claims.sentence: Recent systems take the cited work, retrieved automatically or supplied by the user, locate candidate evidence in it and judge whether it supports the claim \citep{haan2025semanticcite,mocan2026refverifier,sadeghi2026deepsciverify,lee2026reflens,li2026bibagent}; some add a partial-support verdict \citep{haan2025semanticcite,mocan2026refverifier}.
claims.claim: DeepSciVerify retrieves the cited work, extracts relevant passages and judges whether they support the claim.
claims.excerpt: it retrieves the complete paper when available, extracts relevant passages using RAGbased passage retrieval, and produces a final verdict from passage-level evidence.
claims.note: Supported for the clause it is cited for. Its label set is SUPPORTS / CONTRADICTS / NEI, and it is correctly not cited for the partial-support clause.

claims.sentence: Locating the passage is harder in full text than in an abstract: RefVerifier's evidence-localization hit rate was 98\% on abstracts and 68\% on complete papers \citep{mocan2026refverifier}, and in one small evaluation, adding full-text evidence improved verifiers only modestly, which the authors attribute to the difficulty of selecting the most informative passages \citep{sadeghi2026deepsciverify}.
claims.claim: In one small evaluation, adding full-text evidence improved verifiers only modestly, which the authors attribute to the difficulty of selecting the most informative passages.
claims.excerpt:
Abstracts are widely available but often lack the
detail needed to verify citation-level claims, while naively
providing full-text documents leads to only modest improvements (Section 6.3). This suggests that the challenge is not
only retrieving more information, but selecting the parts of
the document most informative for the claim.
claims.location: Sec. 7 Discussion, p. 8; results in Sec. 6.3 Main Results (Table 3), 91-instance SciTance test split
claims.note: Supported. Minor: in Sec. 6.3 full text 'improves most models' but GPT-4 actually decreases (82.2 to 81.3 Micro-F1) and Claude Sonnet 4.6 rises only 81.1 to 82.4, so 'improved verifiers only modestly' matches the authors' own summary but slightly flatters one model; the attribution is a hedged suggestion ('This suggests'), which 'attribute' renders acceptably.
